newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania enlists basketball player for NATO bid.
newsitem.headline: Romania enlists basketball player for NATO bid.

text.p: Romania's drive to enlist support for its longshot bid for early NATO membership has entered the professional sporting arena, using its National Basketball Association star Gheorghe Muresan.

"I just wrote to President Bill Clinton and some influential U.S. senators to tell them of Romania's hopes of being admitted to NATO in the first wave," Muresan told reporters after meeting President Emil Constantinescu.
"Nobody in the NBA knows where Romania is on the world map. They keep looking for us in Yugoslavia or Russia."
Romania has sent an array of ambassadors, including exiled King Michael, fanning out to NATO's 16 member states to win backing ahead of the Alliance's July summit in Madrid.

France, Italy and Canada have expressed support, but the United States and Britain have failed to do so and Germany has been lukewarm. Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic are seen as the ex-communist countries most likely to be admitted first.
Muresan, 26, plays for the Washington Bullets. He is the first Romanian to play in the NBA and is the league's tallest player at 2.36 metres (7 feet, eight inches).
